newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to auction 4.48 pct of Copel shrs.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to auction 4.48 pct of Copel shrs.

text.p: BNDESPar, the investment arm of Brazil's National Development Bank, said it will auction off 4.48 percent of power distributor Copel's capital.
Copel is owned by the southern state of Parana, which holds 63.3 percent of its total capital. It has 2.5 million clients.
In a statement, BNDESPar said will sell 10.8 billion Copel preferred "B" shares for a minimum price of 13.97 reais per 1,000 shares at the Rio de Janeiro Stock Exchange at 1330 local/1630 GMT.
Last year, Copel's net earnings jumped 103.2 percent to 225.3 million reais, from 110.8 million reais in 1995, under the inflation-adjusted accounting method, the statement said.

Garantia, Banco Fator, Omega, Patrimonio, Maxima, BBA Paraibas, Banco da Bahia, Icatu, Bradesco, Banestado, Itau Bankers Trust, Bozano, Simonsen, Liberal, Santander Investment and Banco Votorantim will be brokering the deal, it added.
